open.note: The central he decision; nothing is translated until it is closed. Option 1, gender-free phrasing: verbal-noun buttons, impersonal 'ניתן' / 'יש ל־' / 'באפשרותך', unpointed second-person past, nominal headlines, no present-tense participle aimed at the reader. (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/SpringBoardHome.framework | SpringBoardHome.strings | WIDGET_DISCOVERABILITY_DESCRIPTION); permission bodies use unmarked 'שלך' and 'עבורך' (Applications/FamilyControlsAuthenticationUI.app | Localizable.strings | NOTIFICATION_AUTH_REQUEST_MESSAGE_INDIVIDUAL) and impersonal 'ניתן להפעיל' (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/HealthUI.framework | HealthUI-Localizable.strings | AUTHORIZATION_DONT_ALLOW_ALERT_MESSAGE); the past 2sg is spelled the same for both genders, 'השתמשת' (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | WeeklyReportNotificationGroupSpecifierFooterText). Option 2, masculine second person, is the common Israeli consumer-app default and reads warmer on celebration copy, but it tells a woman the app assumed a man on every badge line; the one Apple string that must pick does pick masculine, 'מבקש' (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE). open.recommended_reason: A badge name is read as a label on the reader, which is the worst place in the app to guess a gender, and the state form keeps the workplace conceit without naming the person.

Option 1 rewrites them as states or events ('התקבלת', 'עברת לשכר חודשי', 'חזרת לתפקיד', 'קביעות'), using the unpointed second-person past that is spelled the same for both genders (iOS 26.1 (23B86) runtime: System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/ScreenTimeSettingsUI.framework | Localizable.strings | WeeklyReportNotificationGroupSpecifierFooterText, 'השתמשת'); the cost is that four names change grammatical shape while the other twenty stay noun phrases. Option 2 keeps role nouns in masculine singular under the gender_strategy default, which is what Apple does on the one string that must pick (System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/UserNotificationsServer.framework | Localizable.strings | USER_NOTIFICATION_PERMISSION_ALERT_TITLE, 'מבקש'). Option 3, 'קביעות', is listed because tenure is the one of the four that already has a gender-free abstract noun, so a mixed answer is possible. The conceit itself travels (משמרת, שכר, חזרה לעבודה); only the reader-labelling nouns do not. Meanwhile no badge name is written at all, because this decision moves with gender_strategy and a batch that guesses one will have to redo the other. open.recommended_reason: No Israeli price is written with a three-letter code, and copy cannot compensate for a formatter.
open.note: Not a wording decision, but it lands on the paywall, insights and widget screens this locale has to write around, which is why it is tracked here. AppCurrency.format reserves .presentation(.narrow) for USD, EUR, JPY and GBP and gives every other code .isoCode (Manifesting/Foundation/Localization/AppCurrency.swift:24-36; formatCompact repeats the same list at :61), so with ILS the app prints '‏120 ‏ILS' where he_IL itself prints '‏120.00 ‏₪' (facts per-locale/he/locale-formats.json money.format_120 and money.locale_standard_120, iOS 26.1 (23B86)). Option 1 adds ILS to the narrow list, an engineering change with a render check on every money surface. Option 2 ships the ISO code with a recorded reason. The option counts here should stay 0 in both columns whatever is decided: no target string ever writes a currency symbol or code, because the placeholder carries the amount (app CLAUDE.md:42), so a non-zero count is itself the finding. Meanwhile agents write neither '₪' nor 'ILS' into a string, and the paywall, insights and widget renders record what the reader actually sees.
